cells.tense: Right now you are carrying some of it for other people, on purpose.
cells.ask: Name one standing arrangement you keep — who it covers, what it costs you — then say out loud whether to keep it, change it, or let it end.
cells.core:
You're someone with something to spare, and you pass it to the people who need it. Not the loud kind. Measured, deliberate, worked out first and then done. When you put your strength toward someone, it's because you decided they were the ones to catch.

What works here is the aim. You can say what this sharing is for, and the people on the other end can feel the intention in it. That's the part worth keeping. So the next move isn't more or less — it's naming what this flow is pointed at, and pointing it. Keeping it fair costs attention. The same attention you already spend giving it out.
cells.sheetLine: You share by measure, and you know what it's for.
cells.verb: sharing what you have so it reaches the ones who need it
cells.place: at the table where what's owed and what's given get weighed

cells.tense: You are living somewhere ahead of now, bracing for a bill nobody has handed you.
cells.ask: Take one account — money, favors, hours — and write the real total. Then leave it alone for a week and see what breaks.
cells.core:
You can hand someone strength and know exactly what it costs, which is the good part of this. That steadiness is what people lean on, and you don't flinch when someone needs a thing from you. Where it bends is that you're already spending against what hasn't happened yet. A favor gets tracked before it's asked. A gift comes with an imagined return attached. You check the scale before the first weight has been set on it.

Holding people up has turned into watching them, and the watching has no end. Nothing you calculate this hard will come out feeling fair, because you're checking faster than anything can settle.
cells.sheetLine: You're auditing fairness before anything has happened.

cells.tense: You used to hand things over easily and you are still standing at that door.
cells.ask: Do one small thing for someone this week, then let it drop — no mention, no accounting, no waiting for a return.
cells.core:
You know how to give, and right now you aren't giving. Nothing's gone wrong with how much you have. It just isn't leaving your hands. What isn't moving is the moment that used to follow a finished thing — the handing over, the putting it down. That moment isn't arriving, so the weight stays in your arms.

With the people who lean on you, you call this being careful rather than generous, and careful isn't what they get. What they get is distance where the handoff used to be. So finish one small thing for someone, then stop carrying it, and let that be the end of your part.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped passing things on and kept carrying them.
cells.verb: sharing what you have so it reaches the ones who need it
cells.place: at the table where what's owed and what's given get weighed

cells.tense: You are the one keeping the exchange even, and you won't claim it.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, something you gave that nobody asked you to give — and don't soften it into 'we all do that.'
cells.core:
You're doing the balancing while it's happening, and you don't call it anything. Someone notices who paid last, who covers when another is short, who keeps the scale from tipping toward them. That someone is you, most times. Out of your mouth it comes out as things simply working out.

When you can name what you gave — the hours, the money, the yes you said for someone else — you can steer it. When you call it the usual thing, it steers you, and you're left holding the tab. There's a claim here that hasn't been made, and only you can make it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it even, and you call it nobody's doing.

attempts.check: Unsupported: that the person is already sharing strength outwardly and merely misdescribing it — the record gives no history, only the shape of the misattribution, so the cell stays inside what could be happening right now. A reader could reasonably object that they are not sharing anything at all, only managing logistics, which is why every ask is one visible act that works whether or not the read is true. The ask survives being wrong because the act (cover a cost, say a number aloud, hold a yes) teaches the same thing either way, and it never promises what it fixes. The sentence that serves the writer is 'resources flowing where needed' — it sounds like the card is doing the giving, so the cells put the giver back in the person's hands.
